sections.what_happened: Jordanian security forces arrested 3 suspects early Monday after finding them hiding in an abandoned house in Karak; the suspects refused to surrender and opened fire, were wounded and arrested, with firearms and ammunition seized; no security personnel were injured. The suspects are linked to Friday's attack in which gunmen opened fire during a funeral at St George's Greek Orthodox Church in Hamoud/Hammoud village, Karak governorate (~120 km southwest of Amman), killing 9 people and wounding 40 (Reuters/CNA/The National figure). King Abdullah II called the attack 'terrorism'; Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said Monday authorities would hold accountable everyone found involved and were examining what led young people toward extremism. The Directorate did NOT identify the suspects' affiliation or say whether they belonged to any militant group; no group has claimed responsibility.
sections.what_verified: Arrests and attack toll corroborated across Reuters (T1, via Jerusalem Post/CNA) and The National (T2), both carrying the Public Security Directorate statement. Attack background (Friday funeral shooting) independently reported by CNN (Oct 23) and Arab News/Reuters.
sections.what_disputed: Casualty-count discrepancy to note, not to resolve here: New Indian Express's Monday summary says 25 wounded, against Reuters/CNA/The National's 40 wounded; the 9-killed figure is consistent across families. Affiliation is explicitly undisclosed - any claim naming a group for this attack is UNVERIFIED at this scan. ABNA's Monday item (Lebanese Shia council condemnation) is reaction, not new evidence on perpetrators.
sections.why_matters: Three arrested, nine dead, zero names: Jordan stopped the Karak gunmen but has not yet said who sent them.
